transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get the sign-off meeting started. We've got the awards-show tribute scheduled for the main stage during Friday's 8 PM live broadcast, and the current draft has two indoor flame jets at the upstage edge with the audience starting 2 meters from the stage. Before I can approve the final effects plan and we can get the stage plot and production certificate issued, we need to work through the review agenda. Rafael, can you confirm the safety configuration for the flame jets and audience positioning? Then Jules, I'll need you to confirm the insurance requirements. Let's make sure everything matches the venue's production policy — the final effects plan needs to align with written approvals and have all insurance documentation in place before the production certificate goes out.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we go further. After inspecting the stage with the fire marshal this morning, I received written event approval for cold-spark units only — exactly four units, positioned at least 3 meters from the audience, operated by a licensed effects operator. The approval has not yet been uploaded to the production file. This means the current draft's two indoor flame jets at the upstage edge with the audience at 2 meters do not match what was actually approved. We need to revise the effects plan to the four cold-spark units at the approved distances before I can confirm the safety configuration.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag an insurance issue. I confirmed with the insurer yesterday that the show is covered for effects only if the cold-spark plan is attached to a filed special-effects endorsement before the broadcast. Right now, the insurer's certificate amendment is still awaiting filing — so the insurance documentation is not yet in place.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Upload the written event approval for four cold-spark units at 3 meters minimum audience distance with licensed operator to the production file.
Revise the effects plan from two indoor flame jets at 2 meters to four cold-spark units at minimum 3 meters audience setback, matching the written approval.
File the special-effects endorsement with the cold-spark plan attached before the Friday 8 PM broadcast so insurance documentation is in place.

Once the approval is uploaded, the effects plan is revised to match, and the insurance endorsement is filed, Morgan will approve the final effects plan so the stage plot and production certificate can be issued.
